phase_name: AESIC-001 Final Contract Repair Independent Verification
summary: Phase 147L.4 independently verified AESIC-001 v1.2 (Phase 147L.3's repair) against the two Non-Blocking findings Phase 147L.2 raised (Finding 3.1: Stage 1 interface-channel gap; Finding 3.2: canonical pointer tamper-evidence gap). Both findings were independently re-derived from primary sources before consulting either prior report's own conclusions, and both are confirmed resolved: Stage1EvaluationResult/AESIC-REQ-122-125/128 give evaluate_stage_2 a complete, validated, closed channel for a caller-retained Stage 1 result; AESIC-REQ-126/127's pointer_digest and mandatory read-time cross-check make the canonical pointer tamper-evident against both corruption variants Phase 147L.2 constructed. This phase's own fresh adversarial pass across the complete, unmodified v1.2 text (all 32 sections, 128 requirements) surfaced two new, independently-derived, Non-Blocking findings neither prior phase examined: Finding A (Major) -- the Stage 2 idempotency no-op branch (AESIC-REQ-023(a), gated by AESIC-REQ-121's equality procedure, which compares only citation_text and AuthorityEvaluationOutcome fields) can return an existing canonical AER unchanged even when the current Stage 2 attempt supplied a genuinely valid, AESIC-REQ-123-validated stage_1_result the existing canonical AER does not carry -- silently defeating AESIC-REQ-057's 'MUST carry stage_1_outcome_ref whenever a valid stage_1_result is supplied' guarantee, an interaction impossible to examine before this repair introduced stage_1_result two revisions after AESIC-REQ-023/121 were last touched; Finding B (Minor) -- Section 11.2's restart matrix, which AESIC-REQ-103 requires to name every restart point, has no explicit row for a crash between the AER's own compound-key commit (AESIC-REQ-119 item 1) and the canonical pointer's own write (AESIC-REQ-119 item 2), a restart point the two-tier storage model itself structurally introduces. Neither new finding reopens Finding 3.1 or Finding 3.2, undermines any other requirement's satisfiability, or affects cross-contract compatibility (independently reconfirmed zero amendments required to AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, or CHGR-001). All fourteen architectural invariants named in the authorizing prompt were independently re-confirmed preserved. fast_green 4391/4391 and the 183 authority-evaluation tests all passed unchanged; no production, schema, test, or runtime file was touched -- this phase performed verification only. Overall Verdict: AESIC-001 v1.2 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS. Per the authorizing prompt's own no-go-unconditional-147M rule, a remaining Major finding means this phase does not recommend proceeding directly to 147M; it recommends a narrowly-scoped repair phase (147L.5) addressing exactly Finding A and Finding B, followed by an independent re-verification (147L.6), before 147M can be considered.

validation_results.result: Directly re-read the complete AESIC-001 v1.2 contract text (all 32 sections, 2392 lines) and both Phase 147L.2's and Phase 147L.3's own reports in full before forming an independent judgment, per this phase's own independence discipline: primary-source reconstruction of both findings performed before consulting either prior report's stated disposition.

validation_results.name: phase_147l4_finding_31_verification
validation_results.result: Independently re-derived Finding 3.1 (Stage 1 interface-channel gap) from AESIC-001 v1.1's own frozen text and independently confirmed AESIC-REQ-122/123/124/125/128 (v1.2) close it completely: Stage1EvaluationResult gives evaluate_stage_2 a validated, optional channel for the exact value AESIC-REQ-118 needs, without widening AES's closed-interface hardening (AESIC-REQ-008) or reopening AES statelessness (AESIC-REQ-017) or the Session non-write-back rule (AESIC-REQ-060).

validation_results.name: phase_147l4_finding_32_verification
validation_results.result: Independently re-derived Finding 3.2 (canonical pointer tamper-evidence gap) and independently confirmed AESIC-REQ-126/127 close both constructed corruption variants (bit-level pointer corruption; a corrupted record_id silently naming a different, valid AER) via pointer_digest plus mandatory read-time cross-check against the referenced AER's own self-carried digest, fail-closed via CanonicalPointerCorruptError.

validation_results.name: phase_147l4_fresh_adversarial_analysis
validation_results.result: Constructed 14 fresh Stage-1-channel adversarial attacks and 14 fresh pointer-integrity adversarial attacks, independently, without reusing Phase 147L.2's or Phase 147L.3's own scenario wording. All but two produced a deterministic, contract-defined, correct result. Two produced new findings: Finding A (idempotency no-op silently discarding a validated stage_1_result, contradicting AESIC-REQ-057) and Finding B (no restart-matrix row for a crash between AER commit and pointer write, though AESIC-REQ-103 requires one).

validation_results.name: phase_147l4_full_consistency_audit
validation_results.result: Re-read AESIC-001 v1.2 in full (not only the repaired sections), checking for contradictions, duplicate definitions, invalid cross-references, undefined terminology, exception-taxonomy inconsistency, lifecycle/replay/persistence contradictions, failure-ownership gaps, security omissions, observability gaps, diagram/example inconsistency, and requirement-matrix inconsistency. One contradiction found (Finding A, AESIC-REQ-057 vs. AESIC-REQ-023(a)/121) and one completeness gap found (Finding B, AESIC-REQ-103 vs. section 11.2's own table). No third issue found.

validation_results.name: phase_147l4_architectural_preservation_check
validation_results.result: Independently re-checked all fourteen invariants named in this phase's own governing prompt (AES sole orchestrator, Decision Template Resolution ownership, Registry lookup-only ownership, evaluator purity/determinism/Registry-exclusion, Stage 1 advisory semantics, Stage 2 unconditional supersession, immutable AER history, canonical-pointer-as-selection-state-only, disclosure-only semantics, non-gating guarantees, replay observational equivalence, Publication Coordinator publication-only ownership, unchanged runtime capability) against AESIC-001 v1.2's current text directly; all confirmed preserved. Replay observational equivalence confirmed for nine of ten independently-checked restart points, with the tenth being Finding B -- a completeness gap, not a demonstrated inequivalence.

validation_results.name: phase_147l4_requirement_matrix

validation_results.name: phase_147l4_cross_contract_verification
validation_results.result: Independently re-confirmed, by direct citation-checking against each predecessor contract's own frozen text (not by trusting AESIC-001's own claims), that AESIC-001 v1.2 requires zero amendments to AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, or CHGR-001.
